¶1 Auzubillah Minashaitan Nirajeem

¶2 Bismillah-ir-Rahman-ir-Rahim

¶3 This piece of hand-out that I have given you is a fascinating piece of literature on human knowledge and types of knowledge which we discussed last week. This is from Al-Futuhat Al-Makkiyaa of Ibn Arabi. It is a type of analysis of Michel Chodkiewicz of Ibn Arabi Al-Futuhat Al-Makkiyaa but it is very beautiful on types of human knowledge and if you remember we have 2 types of knowledge, one knowledge which comes from intellect, reasoning and the other which comes from inside, a type of aqidah, visualising of the soul, the soul captures images and of course what the soul captures is always ilmul khuzuli and what the mind captures is ilmul khuzuli and ilmul husuli both. Now let us see how knowledge is created in human.

¶4 This is a very interesting issue. I don’t know if you have ever thought. You know we see many things. . How this knowledge comes about? Now image of course about the things that you see, fear is a bit difficult to analyse. So now let us see it this way. I want to tell you that god is imagine less. You know even if you didn’t know anything about this concept, now you have come to knowledge which is very superficial. How did this knowledge come about in your mind? If you get anything of what I said.. Sometimes you recite the verses of the Quran and impresses you in a way that you are shaken. Now of course there are different things here which affect you.

¶5 When I want to place a knowledge which is my mind into your mind, what will I do? First of all there is a concept in my mind. There is a picture of what I want to say, an image whether it is an image of a concept or image of a being, image of a visible thing in my mind. I want to put it in your mind. Now this is very interesting. We never have thought about this creation of knowledge in this way. How I can make something in my mind? What I do? I have the image in my mind, when I decide from my heart, a point of decision that I want to convey. Okay I think of an image.

¶6 I decide to transfer that to you which you don’t know anything about it. Suppose you don’t know anything about it and I want to transfer it to you. After I have decided I order the nervous system to create something which corresponds to the image and the nervous system transfers it to my vocal cord. I decide, I shape god and this is the concept. Now this is carried out what actually I have created through my body, it is carried out.. And then it goes to the other way as it has come from me. It goes through your nervous system, then it goes to mind and then it creates an image. In this way I have put a knowledge which is in my mind to your mind.

¶7 Is that true or not? How is it possible through a physical being and feel something in your mind which is not physical? That image is not physical at all. Even the image of a tree in your mind is not physical. It is something which is attached to a non-physical aspect of your mind because it cannot be on that small cell because even if you can go to that very small, tiny particles in your mind, your cells then there should be something which can capture them all together. They are separated from each other, the image which in transferred to your mind, the tree for example. The image which is transferred you say ok it is transferred through my system of visual system.

¶8 I see with my eyes, it is carried to my some cell in my mind which is paired to receive them. It receives them. It is not one call. There are different cells or even if it is a cell it has different parts. It can be divided into different parts. Although we cannot comprehend by one cell or few cells, there is something else. After that image is there it captures it. This is how knowledge is created. Now I transfer knowledge which is inside my mind into your mind in a very easy way. This is very easy of course. Now if you think about it.. the image that I have created through physical means has given rise to spiritual image in your mind because knowledge is not physical.

¶9 When you want to look and search for something you go to yourself, your mind and not the one which takes it out and understands it. This system of human knowledge is fascinating and of course in Islam we have that knowledge only comes from Allah. It is He who actually creates all these things in you of course through many means but it is not a simple thing which comes and I will translate very easy now I very easily place the knowledge and go on at least about what I said. Now you have an understanding which is very vague and have an idea in your mind. There are 2 types of knowledge. One which is acquired knowledge and the other is knowledge with presence.

¶10 Can people place knowledge from heart to heart? Is it true? How is it possible? We don’t have any experience of it. Of course we have experience of placing knowledge from one mind to another mind. But we don’t have the experience of placing knowledge from ones heart to others heart. Imam Ali (as) said when the prophet was on his death bed he said that from which 1000 door of knowledge open to my heart. From each door one thousand other doors open to my heart. It was not that the knowledge was placed on my door. It didn’t come from language. It turned from heart to heart. This is the type of knowledge which the urafaa have knowledge coming not from mind to mouth but from heart.

¶11 And if not from heart to heart or from heart to heart might be difficut of course urafaa says you cannot receive directly from god to your heart. It is possible but it is very difficult. You usually have to get through someone else to start. Now in Shia belief what we say that whatever knowledge about god we receive comes from the imam. Although you don’t realise it comes through a means to your heart. So read the article about knowledge. It is very important because we don’t think how our knowledge comes about and we think that our knowledge is just provision here and there and we put them together. We do not realise. It is difficult. It is something which is completely monopolized by Allah.

¶12 Have you read this verse I had mentioned you think about this. This is fascinating. I real try to and recite this verse. This is at the end of Surah Hashr, “Huwal Laahul Khaaliqul Baari 'ul Musawwir; lahul Asmaaa'ul Husnaa; yusabbihu lahoo maa fis samaawaati wal ardi wa Huwal 'Azeezul Hakeem”59:24 Allah is khaliq. Khaliq means to compose things together and create something out of them. Of course he brought everything from adam but usually khalaq means composing things together, creating one thing from another. We are also khaliq by the way okay. Why he needs to bring something out of nothing? He is the one who created the soul out of nothing. As we are also Khaliq, it is actually a gift of god.

¶13 Had it been placed in us or not? Of course usually some exegesis especially the urafaa they say “Wa 'allama Aadamal asmaaa'a kullahaa” 2:31it means that Allah has put that flavour of all his abilities into us, a flavour of all his abilities. That’s why he is Khaliq and we are also Khaliq. He is Bari meaning he decreed things out of nothing. He placed it this way. Al-Bari as well. You just decide to create something in your mind out of nothing. You can do that. You are Bari as well. There is a hadith which states that Allah has created Adam after his own image. Means Adam can do whatever Allah does in a certain way especially when we go to Janna inshaAllah you will see how similar we are with those aspects of Allah which could be actually compared because some aspects or some level completely of Allah are completely different.

¶14 No mind can ever think about it. And sometime we talk about human relation with creation and so we have some similarities of his abilities in ourselves. There is another hadith which says that whoever knows his soul knows Allah. One of the meanings is that your soul is created after his own image. You know yourself you know Allah. It is a simplest way of explaining it of course you are servant, you are abdh, you are nothing and you are just like an imagination in the mind so to speak. But he has completely created you out of his knowledge. But there are certain things which are completely monopolised by him. Now somewhere as well giving image to things, giving shape and colors to things are Al-Musaawir as well.

¶15 Now even I your mind and your imagination you are Al-Musawwir. You can only image those things that you have already seen. And image when you compose things, I mean you create something completely new inner material but you have experience of .. You can create a horse with wings but you should have seen wings and horses and put them together. You can create new color but you can create only create and outcome of what you have seen. It is only He who is Al-Musawwir. Just imagine out of nothing he has created all these images. It is not for us to imagine. We cannot imagine. We can only imagine colour, shapes and things, all of them have come out of nothing.

¶16 We have a hadith mentioned in Nahjul Balgha that there was no experience before Allah would make that image after he had fashioned. It is impossible. He creates everything and he has fashioned it. He gives taswir. We have this term Al-Musawwir or Al-Musawwarakum. It is just to bring about out of nothing. Bari means maker but Al-musawwir means giving all those things which are out of nothing a taswir ie shapes, colour, images. We cannot do it. May be in jannah we can be Al-Musawwir but I don’t know. We have in hadith that you obey me, I will make you like musawwir. So if this hadith is to be taken to reflect we cannot of course say on the Day of Judgment that O God!

¶17 We obeyed you so I want to be Al-Musawwir. You are Al-Musawwir so I also want to be Al-Musawwir. The prophet said that we did not worship you as much you deserved to be worshipped. So no one can say and no one can create anything but of course when he said it, he said it with rational meaning you follow in human capacity and then of course I will make you like Al-Musawwir. And that’s why not many people could reach that level. If you want to become Al-Musawwir and you always make evil images, he wants to give you all these powers but the powers can be only given to those who do not want to be arrogant.

¶18 You obey him in fact because he is so pure, Al-Quddus that whenever we commit a sin, you get an awakening. Think about that in this way. He is so pure that he cannot accept impurity in the soul. He is Al-Malikil Quddus and we all say that we want to have place inside of purity and cleanness and of course that will be difficult to attain and think about the type of knowledge that Allah puts in the heart of people. You talk about how knowledge can be heart to heart and Allah to us. It is only Allah who puts the knowledge in the heart. We have in hadith that Knowledge is not (acquired) through extensive learning. Rather, it is the light that God sends in the heart of whomever He wishes to guide.

¶19 Verily knowledge consists of these three: the ‘firm sign’, the ‘just duty’ and the ‘established sunnah (method)’. All else is superfluous. This is the gate to knowledge of course if you see the whole verse and we put a light by which he would understand and realise what people are. Is he equal with the one who is completely in darkness and can’t come out of it? Well, the light comes to the heart on the pure ones and the darkness covers impure ones. I just wanted to mention about this knowledge of irfan after they have been taken out of knowledge. It is not something that you can read anywhere. It is not something that you can find out that’s why it comes through suluk.

¶20 The knowledge that you learn in university or hawza or whatever it comes through fikr. You think, you put it together, you analyse, you find out. The knowledge that comes to us is through suluk which is the heart with purity and can say suluk is a path to purity or striving towards purification. You purify yourself and then wait for Allah to put the light in your heart. The light is everywhere. “Allaahu noorus samaawaati wal ard” 24:35 but your heart is closed. By suluk you want to open it so that the light shines in you. That’s all. It is not the case that Allah choses people to give light in the heart. His light is everywhere. He is with you wherever you are.

¶21 The only thing is that you have to open the heart, let the light go through. That’s all. What the urafaa are after tis to find a way to open the heart and let the light go in. The urafaa are after this to find a way to open the heart and when the heart opens the light goes in and shines. That’s what we usually say. There is no hindrance or framing from the side of Allah to pour his knowledge, bounty and nemah on you. It is all there. So it is for us to find it to let it come in. If you remember we mentioned that we have ilm and maarifah. Of course as I said in religious terminology these 2 things are wrong because when they say ilm it means maarifah.

¶22 They don’t consider other types of ilm to be real ilm. When they say ilm it means the maarifah actually. People are of 2 kinds, the one who knows knowledge about god; it means the one who has maarifah and the other who tries to learn it. Urafaa says it us. The immah the prophets they are aalemul ulema and then the urafaa says we want to learn and understand idrak. Means you learn time and space and with limits. Without the limit you cannot have knowledge of anything. You have to synchronise, you have to limit and analyse and for analysing you have to make things in a different limits and analyse it. Now maarifah is a usooli where you arrive at somewhere.

¶23 It’s not that you try to find out, you just find and arrive. It is the inside and the self-purification and if you lose you lose faith because if you want to find the limits of Allah and if you put limitations you cannot find Allah. Now one other difficulty here, Ibn Sina, the master of philosophy and towards the end of his life he was the master of irfan because after Ibn Sina met Abu Said Abul Khayr, a great mystic of his own time, he completely changed. Ibu Sina towards the end of his life writes a letter to Abu Said Abul Khayr and says I will learn from you, teach me from the knowledge that you have.

¶24 Of course Ibn Sina was a genius. No one ever though that Ibn Sina is going to learn something familiar. You know at the age of 15-16 no philosopher could ever compete with Ibn Sina and then of course Ibn Sina Said writes in that thesis that of course you have high knowledge. How can I teach you something? But of course then he teaches him many things. And in Isharat he writes, I will give you that part on irfan in Isharat wal-Tanbihat. Now it is taught by most urafa in Qum and they say we don’t have any chapter better than this written by Ibn Sina. Ibn Sina was not an aarif but his mind was so bright that just with a visit and correspondence with Abu Said Abul-Khayr he wrote that very nice article on what are irfan and maqamatul aarifeen and the stations of the urafaa.

¶25 He says that understanding the knowledge of ..is beyond human capacity. What you know of the object is but the characteristics with the … and their attributes. Actually means something which accidentally have attached to other things. It might be there in my mind. So does anyone know what does Ibn Sina wants to say? It is beyond human capacity to know the .. of course this was before he wrote that maqamat. It is impossible to know. You only now what actually lies down this entity in terms of colours, dimension and functions. All these things we know but to certain extent. But you don’t really know what is the thing which all these come upon it. “Khalaqal laahus samaawaati wal arda bilhaqq” 29:44 mystics have great elaborate discussion on what is this haqq with which Allah has created things.

¶26 Haqq is reality of everything. Everything is created now for one instance out of that haqq you can never know what that haqq is. If you say this is made of this thing. It has dimension, this colour. If you did it but what is that thing which you are talking about? This wajood. You cannot know. It is impossible for you, for your knowledge, your mind. You cannot grasp it. There is no dimension or colour nothing that you can attribute to it. How do you know god? It is impossible to know god because there is no characteristic. No dimension, no color, no use that you can think of. You cannot know the essence of anything. The only way the different aspects and characteristics that you know, now if you cannot know any characteristics about god, is it that we don’t know or we can’t know?

¶27 This is what Ibn Sina says, it is beyond human capacity. You cannot know god because your mind cannot analyse but not have any dimension or colour.

¶28 Now let's see what Mullah Sadra says. You have heard about Mulla Sadra, haven't you? He is the philosopher which changed the whole course of Islamic philosophy from hikmatul mashaal to hikmatul mutaaal. It could only be achieved by inner faculty by human soul. It is only possible to know the reality by ilmul khuzuli which your soul could capture to cover. It’s the only possible way. And this is the only way that you could know God. It is the only way. You say and have other arguments saying that God exists. But you can only say this. But what is God, you cannot say. It's beyond human capacity in that aspect. Mulla Sadra says the reality of the truth would be more true with..

¶29 the reality of course being of the wujood. Now, they say wujood is equivalent to god. Of course, it's not as easy to think that you are God or a part of God. It's utter nonsense. However, they say any wajood is a manifestation of god, any existence could not be known except through its characteristics. However, if you want to know the reality of it, your soul is … The eyes cannot catch him. It is the heart which gives reality to faith. The only way to know god is faith. Faith for us is a much diluted type of knowledge. We believe in him and if we move up on the scale of faith it's like your eyes might be very weak.

¶30 You cannot see colour very properly unless you use spectacles. You heart might be weak and you cannot see God. Now think god in reality. It’s mentioned that on the Day of Judgment some people look at Allah. And in Munajat-e-Muhibeen we have that, give me the favour of looking at you. Now this is the reality and this is one of the most astonishing things put in human being. And it's only human. A weaker type of this knowledge is put in everything. That's why they say on the day of Judgement, when human knowledge gets very, very strong other objects get to access enough knowledge which might be that human knowledge in this world. Everything gets stronger in terms of faith and knowledge of Allah.

¶31 Speak out and talk about things that he had witnessed. That is not because the earth has a speciality. Everything has become stronger in understanding. Now of course, even a leaf on the tree has an understanding and knowledgeable about god but it's very weak. It's not comprehensible at all. On the Day of Judgment they wake up and we wake up. And our knowledge improves, their knowledge improves. It's not only us that are speaking. Everything on the day speaks but in their own way. Now on the Day of Judgment.. speaks as well but they need a strong type of soul that could make them speak. Allah on the Day of Judgment makes everyone speak, isn’t it? It’s mentioned in Nahjul Balagha that the kuffar wanted a miracle from the prophet and they told him if you make this tree witness your prophethood we would believe in you and imam explains it in very nice way.

¶32 He himself has witnessed this. Then the prophet said do you really believe in this tree giving shahadah? He said yes. All the trees on the authority of being the Prophet of God, I ask you to witness what you have to witness and the imam speaks that the trees in a very eloquent way started to recite Qalamah.

¶33 It is very easy for Allah to make everything speak. For us it is impossible but inshaAllah when you move on the way of suluk you would see numerous miracles. The prophet is the khalifa and khalifa means someone who taught him or someone put him in charge. Now the prophets are not after proving Allah or wanting to say for example say things about Allah .. They want real feeling, experience and knowledge of Allah, a positive and not a negative knowledge. What we know about Allah is negative knowledge. Allah cannot be an object. Allah cannot be in a place and not in another place. Allah cannot be this; Allah cannot be that, this is negative knowledge. But what Allah is?

¶34 It could be actually grasped by the soul. Man'arafa nafsahu 'arafa rabbah. Whoever knows his soul knows god because the soul can bring that knowledge into itself. It is given that knowledge and of course that knowledge has degrees. Allah’s knowledge increases, the more you go the thirstier you'll become. The more you know, the more bewildered you will become. And that's why mystics are like mad people. They are completely immersed. People say that they are really immersed, something had limited their understanding and ….. and they are ill because they cannot concentrate as other people can concentrate because they are completely absorbed in the greatness. Now, how is this possible? If true knowledge is given to our heart which is actually the center of the soul for understanding and knowledge, of course heart and soul has a difference.

¶35 InshaAllah we will discuss this later on. So I think it's enough. At this stage, to know the difference between the knowledge that we seek in irfan and the knowledge which we seek in philosophy or science. In philosophy, science and these things we analyse things. We limit them. We make them into units and we want to know their characteristics, their accidents, their colouring. In irfan we want to know the unity. We want to know God in his unity. So what is the irfan? …. the subject matters which is called Mawzooq. It has its own principles and it's questions. Anytime of course, traditionally all the philosophers and scientists approach any knowledge they approach it to these 3 categories.

¶36 What is the subject? For example, when you want to study physics, what is the subject matter of physics? What is? And then what are its principles on which you base your arguments? And then what are the questions that you are asking. What you want to know? Now the subject matter of every science is that thing which we discussed is immediate accident in that time. So for example say in Maths …..They say every object has an essence, which is of course is essential part and other things which are not essential they can be there or they cannot. Like … its colour is an accident. Accidentally it is brown, but it could have been any other colour.

¶37 So an accident is something which is accidently so to speak. It could have been otherwise. So we think about immediate accident, therefore, that thing which is called maroof which is the very essence is the subject and the subject and the accident are the questions and principles. What other colour can we give to it? What other shape and other dimensions can we give to its essence? So these are the questions. Now principles of the self-evident as humanistic and priority issues and accidents. Now, there are some accidents which go with this. Usually is that it could be detached, but usually it there. And we build our question around that and the questions of any kind are those issues in need of discussion, exploration and further understanding.

¶38 Now what is the subject matter of irfan? To discuss or to find out about of course, we don't find it through the ordinary means which is fiqh. But what is it that we want to find? Reality or in other words God. We want to know God. So the subject matter of irfan is God and his attributes. This is one of the sentences of Ibne Arabi. We cannot know the essence of god and we cannot understand god. But we want to know him. Actually, we want to know his primordial attributes and his eternal characteristics, his positive theology and not negative. What god is not, but what God is. Do we have positive theology in Quran? Rahman and Rahim, but how can he be Rahman Rahim if he does not move.

¶39 It is not in any sense inhuman by what he creates. How could he be Rahman and Rahim? How could he be forgiving? Why for him to forgive there should be a sin and infact that sin should motivate him to forgive, isn't it? How is it possible? We would know later inshaAllah when we come to positive theology whilst the negative theology. Now, in theology, of course, they take pains to answer this question, but in irfan of course, they have a different method. And that's why I put irfan also has its own theology, but it is not through analytical knowledge, so to speak. Through finding is too unveiling, they say this is a knowledge which comes from illumination of the heart rather than something that you analyse.

¶40 Now this knowledge is possible. And of course, the knowledge of the prophet we know is likely. They knew god. It wasn't analytical knowledge about it was a knowledge which was somehow present in prophet’s heart. So the principles are obvious acronyms. The terminology that we use they are no axiom that really you could build on except what you find unbeatable or something like that, experience of god and that they put it as an acronym and everyone accepts it and then they ask other questions about it. The questions of this science or of this type of knowledge are very difficult. They are rich. You cannot find it, but I mean, and when they explain it to you cannot understand.

¶41 It's impossible for me unless you see it, you cannot do it. How diverse it comes from God. It is weak, no time would initiate anything. How it returns to unity? How diversity goes back to unity, how unity creates diversity. How different manifestations of his name create things in this world? And what is the way towards him? How we can go and find out? This is another branch of irfan. We will discuss about it. Let's see what we have in our hades which are very happening and we will learn about Allah and cannot be understood except by an experience through an unveiling, through a passion. This is one of the khutbas of Imam Ali (as), it's not mentioned in Nahjul Balagha but the similar meaning is mentioned in Nahjul Balagha.

¶42 This is reported by Al Mansoori. You are purified. You are distanced away from everything. How can we understand that? You are away from and nothing ever misses. And I ask for your name which is filled by the essence of everything. This is difficult to understand. But it is a knowledge which is different from our type of knowledge of Allah. Of course, this is what the philosophers say. The reality is that it’s undivided and this is what Ibne Arabi uses. He is manifested, he is hidden. You see, he's everywhere, but still you see nowhere. It is not understandable unless you grasp a way of unveiling your heart. Should we go into pains to go through or actually have to find what Allah is in this way?

¶43 You obey him, it is that not enough? Why should we go to him? A type of putting ourselves in difficulty to find out what Allah is. Is anyone who is interested in this?

¶45 Ans: But not everyone has a question. I mean, there are many people who have no question at all. It needs a very strong power that you actually distract yourself from your immediate pleasures. I want to go for something, a drive which comes out of love. You find out that you cannot understand in this way. So you don’t want to go into this.

¶46 Q2. Not Audible

¶47 Ans: It is put in the heart. First the drive comes and then the awakening comes. Then comes the tawbah and of course when he puts his looks on you but he doesn't choose you unless he loves you. So before you even think about all these you have to purify to the degree. Now when we talk about irfan we say that the first you have to polish your soul by whatever the prophet has demanded from you. This is the first step, without this there is no maarifah. About mojizat, moharramaat, mustahabat, makhluqat and all these things in the hope that Allah will chose you. And when he chooses you then of course it takes you to the other world.

¶48 Those who strive to in their way and then of course we got it. Now find something if you go to an aarif and say give me some sort of advice. What should I do? Well, they cannot. If God cannot guide you then no one can guide you. “famai yahdee man adallal laahu” 30:29 But who will guide those whom Allah leaves astray. He really leaves you astray in the sense that he doesn't let you find your way through him. It's like letting a prisoner to find a way out of a prison. You have to do something so that you are forgiven from the consequences of your sentence and come out. So the drive comes after you have followed the prophet.

¶49 “Yaaa aiyuhal lazeena aamanus tajeeboo lillaahi wa lir Rasooli izaa da'aakum limaa yuhyeekum” 8:24 O ye who believe! Give your response to Allah and His Messenger, when He called you to that which will give you life. Now this life would come when you follow completely what the Prophet says and then wait for the help of the Allah. Don't look for anyone or anything. Correct, rectify your soul and wait.

And I can put guidance from my heart into your heart. So the guidance always comes from Allah and the rest comes from shaitan. But it finds its way you see guidance find those who are prepared for it and what sort of find those who are prepared? Now think about this verse, I think I mentioned this before. “Wa mai ya'shu 'an zikrir Rahmaani nuqaiyid lahoo Shaitaanan fahuwa lahoo qareen” 43:36 If anyone withdraws himself from remembrance of (Allah) Most Gracious, We appoint for him an evil one, to be an intimate companion to him.

It's very difficult to take this chance when they come. Of course, Allah always helps. Always helps but it is remembrance of Allah which drives them back. ¶56 Q5. Not Audible

¶57 Ans: Yeah, probably and there is a very interesting verse. “Bal naqzifu bilhaqqi 'alal baatili fa yadmaghuhoo fa izaa huwa zaahiq; wa lakumul wailu mimmaa tasifoon” 21:18 this is what Allah does. What shaytan does, it wants to bring down haq. It is just an image. It's just a mirage but when haq comes it crushes the latter. Look for example our prophet came he really vanquished batil. In Nahjul Balagha Imam Ali (as) says, I heard a type of crying voice and I asked what this? The prophet said that it was shaytan who cried out because he’s disappointed. He was disappointed when this haq came. And it's got inside every human being depending which side you go. The side towards Allah it strong.

¶58 The only thing is that our himmat is very weak. If he makes an effort, then of course we see that how strong is that.

¶59 Now this is another phase from Nahjul Balagha. He is a being, but not through phenomenon of coming into being. He exists but not from non-existence. He is with everything but not in physical nearness. He is different from everything but not in physical separation. He acts but without connotation of movements and instruments because all actions come to movement either spiritual movement or physical movement. He sees even when there is none to be looked at from among His creation. He is only one, such that there is none with whom He may keep company or whom He may miss in his absence. He initiated creation most initially and commenced it originally, without undergoing reflection, without making use of any experiment, without innovating any movement, and without experiencing any aspiration of mind.

¶60 Can you say you have knowledge of this? No, we don't because this is not a knowledge that could be understood by mind. It's a knowledge that should be understood by your soul, the heart. And what we will go through inshaAllah next week, we will see what human soul is and how it is possible to get the knowledge without this mediation of mind. How is it possible and how is it possible for us to go to that world of Allah.

¶61 Q6. Not Audible

¶62 Ans: Well, it has 2 meanings. One meaning is that they are some sort of thing which invokes the concept in your mind. This is the concept of their creation in this regard. There's another meaning because in that sense you cannot differentiate between the 2 … However, there's another aspect to it and that is they actually reflect the attributes of Allah. That is another meaning of the sound which mystic actually stress upon. They reflect essence, flavour and attributes of Allah.

¶63 Wa sallahu ala mohammadin wa aale hittahereen.
